title: Viewing a Rental at the End of Phuket's Rainy Season: 9 Things to Check
excerpt: October is the best month to see how a Phuket house copes with rain. Nine things to check at a viewing, from ceiling stains and mould to the drains on the soi, before you sign a lease for high season.
author: Islander Home Team
content:
Phuket's rainy season typically runs from May to October, with October usually among the wettest months. High season begins in November, when most people want to move in. That makes the next few weeks an ideal time to view rental properties: you can see exactly how a house holds up in the rain.

Here is what to look out for.

1. Stains on the ceiling

Check the ceiling in every room, especially beneath flat roofs, balconies above, or bathrooms on the floor above. Brown rings or bubbling paint can indicate water damage. Ask whether the problem has been fixed and when the repairs were carried out.

2. Mould and smell

Open the wardrobes and check behind the curtains and the bed. Black spots or a musty smell can indicate persistent damp. A dehumidifier and good airflow can help, but if a room smells of mould in October, the problem is likely to return every rainy season.

3. The drains on the soi

If possible, walk along the road outside after a heavy shower. Some low-lying sois flood for a few hours after a storm, which can be a problem if you drive to work or school. Ask the neighbours or security guard about local flooding. Some listings mention it directly; one pool villa near Laguna is advertised as being in a flood-free area.

4. Water around the doors and windows

Check the floor beneath sliding doors and the sills under windows. Swollen wooden frames, rust on aluminium tracks, or tide marks on the tiles can indicate where rainwater gets in during strong winds.

5. The garden and the slope

If the property is on a hillside in Rawai, Kata or Kathu, inspect the retaining walls and the ground above the house. Cracks or soil washing onto the driveway are worth asking about. On flat land, check whether the garden drains properly or tends to collect standing water.

6. Air-conditioner drains

Each air-conditioning unit has a pipe that carries water away. If water drips onto a terrace, a wall or a neighbour's garden, it can cause damp. Turn on each unit and check where the water drains.

7. The pool

A pool that overflows during heavy rain needs a functioning overflow drain. Ask who cleans the pool, how often it is cleaned, and whether the cost of chemicals after a storm is included in the rent.

8. Termites and insects

Termites often swarm after rain. Look for small piles of wings near lights and windows, or mud tunnels along walls and door frames. Ask whether the house has a termite treatment contract. Window screens also make a big difference in keeping mosquitoes out during the wet months.

9. Power and water

Storms can cause brief power cuts. Ask whether the house has a water pump and tank to keep the water running when mains pressure drops, and check that outdoor sockets and lights are properly covered.

Write it into the lease

Photograph anything you find and agree in writing, before paying the deposit, on who will fix it and by when. This also protects you at the end of the lease. Our lease checklist covers the rest.
